artifacts.summary: Nine-phase plan to author sixteen books-domain context documents plus a navigation README under agent-system/extensions/books/context/project/books/ and register all seventeen in index-entries.json with deliberate Tier 2 / Tier 4 tiering.

memory_candidates.content: Authoring a multi-file domain context corpus for a Claude agent-system extension requires deliberate load_when tiering, decided at plan time rather than inherited from the navigation stub it replaces. The derived-tier rule (validate-context-budgets.sh: always -> Tier 1, agents non-empty -> Tier 2, commands/task_types non-empty -> Tier 3, all-empty -> Tier 4) means a stub entry carrying load_when.agents is Tier 2 and eagerly loaded into every matching dispatch. Reusing that shape for N 150-250-line documents injects the whole corpus into every dispatch. Correct pattern: the README index stays Tier 2 as the single discovery entry point; each document is Tier 4 with load_when hooks empty and on_demand:true (the explicit-intent marker that exempts it from the Dead Entry Check, which is keyed on on_demand precisely because tier is derived). Critically, the budget CAPS table covers only ten named agents, so an all-Tier-2 registration of a new extension's corpus fires no cap and is NOT caught mechanically -- the tiering must be verified by reading back each entry's derived tier (validate-context-budgets.sh --index <extension>/index-entries.json), not by trusting the gate. Also: index-entries.json sits at the extension root, outside any context/ scope glob, yet is the only place new context files can be registered -- registration is inseparable from authoring a context file.
